note: Polyurethane observer-band foaming + foam-mechanics response surface (macro). Maps the nano reagent descriptors to the coefficients of (a) a reduced dual-reaction foaming model and (b) the mechanics of the network it builds, both integrated by the hook layer. Chemistry: gel (urethane) and blow (water-isocyanate) rate constants at the initial temperature, the Arrhenius activation temperature, per-reaction full-conversion exotherms, the ambient heat-loss rate, the through-material heat diffusion rate (which gives a curing bun a hot core and a cooler skin), the CO2 expansion capacity and dissolution-saturation fraction (the induction that delays the visible cream), the Flory gel-point conversion, the Castro-Macosko viscosity growth exponent, the surfactant baseline bubble-trapping efficiency, the volume expansion mobility, the urethane autocatalysis gain, and the conversion at which the network is fully rigid. Mechanics: the bonded-network specific stiffness, the tensile failure strain at which a bond cracks permanently, the reference stress-relaxation (creep) rate that lets a still-fluid resin flow and a cured one lock, structural damping, contact friction and restitution for pieces landing on the table, and the cell-scale IMPERFECTION dispersion that makes no two parcels grow or hold at the same rate. NO expansion ratio, cream/rise/gel/solid time, colour, final consistency, lean angle, crack, fragment count, or landing site is an output here: whether the mixture foams, how far it rises, how hot it gets, whether it leans, whether overhanging pieces crack off and where they fall, and whether it freezes into a rigid sponge all EMERGE from integrating the model under standard gravity, and are graded against known polyurethane-foam behaviour only at run end. This compact response surface is illustrative rather than held-out metrology; its uncertainty is emitted and a wider trained reactive-foam panel is tracked in ROADMAP.md.
